simple.meaning: מַתְּנָא (mattᵉnâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “gift.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַתְּנָא (H4978) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:6, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַתְּנָא (H4978) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַתְּנָא (H4978) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַתְּנָא (mattᵉnâʼ) / H4978 is traced through Daniel 2:6, Daniel 2:48, Daniel 5:17 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4978. mattena [ מַתְּנָא ] noun feminine gift ; — plural absolute מַתְּנָן Dan 2:6 , 48 ; suffix מַתְּנָתָךְ 5:17 .

occurrences.englishText: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you will receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.”
Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.
Then Daniel answered before the king, “Let your gifts be to yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
